description: Authoritative migration risk classification registry, keyed by migration NAME (not version - this repo's deploy tool stamps its own apply-time version, so filename timestamp is not a reliable key; see docs/release/PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_RECONCILIATION.md). Populated for future/release-relevant migrations only, per Phase 1 discovery's instruction not to retroactively hand-edit all historical migrations. A migration present in security/release/migration-baseline.json but absent here is UNCLASSIFIED_HISTORICAL (grandfathered, non-blocking). A migration absent from BOTH files is UNCLASSIFIED_NEW and blocks manifest freeze until an entry is added here. Explicit human/agent classification here is authoritative over security/release/classify-migration-risk.js's static pattern detector, which is advisory only.

provider_request_security.rationale: 3 new tables, 4 new SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, seed INSERT. No pre-existing object touched.

provider_request_security_revoke_anon.rationale: Revokes EXECUTE on 4 functions created in the same PR's prior migration. Tightening, not touching any pre-existing object.

provider_request_security_fix_trigger_se.rationale: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adding only `set search_path = public`; no behavior change.

provider_request_ttl_tuning.rationale: Two bounded, row-scoped UPDATEs on a config table (2 rows total). Not unbounded data transformation.

harden_public_rpc_execution_grants.rationale: REVOKE campaign across 9 pre-existing RPCs plus a CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION on get_item_reaction_counts adding an authorization predicate. Access-tightening on functions, not schema/data changes; reversible by re-granting or reverting the function body.

harden_public_rpc_execution_grants_trigg.rationale: Follow-up REVOKE closing a gap the prior migration in the same PR left open on 9 trigger functions.

image_ingestion_quarantine_storage.rationale: New storage bucket + new insert-only policy. No pre-existing bucket/policy touched.

image_ingestion_clean_storage.rationale: New storage bucket + new select-only policy.

image_scan_verdicts.rationale: New table + RLS + REVOKE/GRANT, all scoped to the new table.

edge_function_errors.rationale: New internal-schema table + REVOKE/GRANT, all scoped to the new table.

legal_acceptances.rationale: Explicitly a recovered-migration-source provenance repair (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, idempotent DROP POLICY IF EXISTS + recreate), not a new schema change. No down-migration is meaningful for a provenance repair.

reconcile_deletion_requests_to_productio.rationale: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS x3, all nullable, no backfill required (author-confirmed safe against the then-2 existing staging rows).

legal_documents_bucket_parity.rationale: Idempotent storage.buckets upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) to match a production parity finding.

production_live_derived_can_react_to_dre.rationale: Reproduces a function that already existed live but had no migration source, via verbatim pg_get_functiondef reproduction. Includes REVOKE/GRANT stated to match already-live production grants exactly.

dressing_room_user_blocking.rationale: Highest-risk file in the Phase 1 sample: new table, additive nullable column, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION on 4 pre-existing load-bearing SECURITY DEFINER functions with materially changed bodies, and DROP POLICY + recreate on two populated tables (dressing_rooms, content_reports). Classified REVERSIBLE, not DESTRUCTIVE, because no DDL removes data or columns - but it is the one migration in the sample with a dedicated hand-authored rollback runbook (20260806153233_dressing_room_user_blocking_ROLLBACK.md), and that runbook's own down-steps are labeled data-destructive. Treat this migration's future promotion as requiring the REVERSIBLE class's tested-explicit-recovery gate to be genuinely satisfied, not rubber-stamped.
dressing_room_user_blocking.reviewFlag: has a companion rollback doc whose down-path is destructive; recovery-plan testing should exercise that doc, not merely acknowledge it exists

harden_trigger_function_search_path.rationale: ALTER FUNCTION ... SET search_path on 4 functions. Config-only, no body/signature change.

enforce_rpc_privilege_boundary.rationale: ~20 REVOKE EXECUTE statements (tightening only, author's own audit confirms every affected RPC already internally guarded on auth.uid()) plus one GRANT (`grant usage on schema internal to authenticated`) that fixed a real fail-closed regression shipped by the prior migration in this same window. Net effect is access tightening / bug fix, not data or schema change.

revoke_public_execute_on_saved_scans_tri.rationale: Single REVOKE EXECUTE closing a PUBLIC-role grant. Tightening only.

apple_auth_credentials.rationale: New table only (create table if not exists public.apple_auth_credentials), plus RLS enable, REVOKE from anon/authenticated, GRANT to service_role, and one new index â€” every statement scoped to the new table. No pre-existing object is touched. Same shape as image_scan_verdicts. Holds one encrypted secret per user with RLS on and deliberately no policies, so anon/authenticated match zero rows; the FK to auth.users cascades on delete as a safety net behind the explicit revoke-then-erase path.

legal_acceptances_restore_ai_processing.rationale: Drops and recreates legal_acceptances_acceptance_type_check on the PRE-EXISTING public.legal_acceptances table to widen the allowed set to include 'ai_processing'. Not EXPANSION_SAFE, because a pre-existing object is modified. Not REVERSIBLE in practice: the widening is strictly more permissive so it cannot fail on existing rows, but the inverse re-narrowing would fail as soon as one ai_processing acceptance has been recorded â€” which is exactly what the restored consent contract writes. Renumbered from the Android lineage's 20260805120000, which is already occupied here by deletion-request reconciliation.

privacy_request_rate_limits.rationale: New table + RLS + SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Contains one flagged runtime pattern (a probabilistic, table-wide-but-WHERE-bounded DELETE inside a hot request-path RPC) that is not itself destructive DDL but is worth static-detector coverage - see classify-migration-risk.js RISK_PATTERNS.
privacy_request_rate_limits.reviewFlag: embedded DELETE inside a client-triggered RPC path; bounded by WHERE + low execution probability, not unqualified

backfill_legacy_pending_deletion_request.rationale: One-time idempotent UPDATE of existing public.deletion_requests rows: legacy status='pending' lifecycle rows are transitioned to 'deactivated' with a grace deadline of greatest(requested_at + 30 days, now() + 7 days), plus an append-only ledger entry per row. No DDL: no table, column, constraint, index or function is created, altered or dropped. DATA_TRANSFORMING rather than EXPANSION_SAFE because pre-existing rows are rewritten, and rather than REVERSIBLE because the prior per-row status is not retained anywhere outside the deletion_state_transitions ledger.
backfill_legacy_pending_deletion_request.recoveryPath: The ledger is the recovery path: every transition is written to public.deletion_state_transitions with from_state='pending', to_state='deactivated' and reason_code='LEGACY_PENDING_BACKFILL', so the exact set of affected request ids and their prior state can be reconstructed and reverted row by row. Scope is bounded to rows that were status='pending' with a non-null user_id and no purged_at/restored_at.
backfill_legacy_pending_deletion_request.reviewFlag: Bounded UPDATE on a lifecycle table. Intentional: leaving these rows in 'pending' is itself the defect -- every governed path (peek/rotate/restore and the purge candidate query) requires 'deactivated', so a pending row is locked out, not restorable and not purgeable.

wardrobe_wear_event_items.rationale: Adds public.wardrobe_wear_event_items (new table, RLS + GRANTs + indexes) and two additive nullable columns on public.wardrobe_wear_events (saved_look_id FK ON DELETE SET NULL, saved_look_ref text). Also DROPS NOT NULL on the pre-existing wardrobe_wear_events.source_item_id so an outfit-level wear need not elect a single garment, replacing it with a CHECK requiring identity from source_item_id, saved_look_id or saved_look_ref. Classified FORWARD_FIX_ONLY rather than REVERSIBLE because that NOT NULL cannot be restored once any outfit-level event exists: those rows carry a null source_item_id by design, so re-narrowing would require deleting real wear history or fabricating a source item for it. No data is transformed and no column is dropped; Build 28 writers are unaffected because they always supply source_item_id.

harden_wardrobe_wear_anon_privileges.rationale: Privilege-layer only. REVOKE ALL ... FROM anon, public on public.wardrobe_wear_events and public.wardrobe_utility_items, then re-GRANT select/insert/update/delete to authenticated exactly as 20260704175544_free_tier_utility_tables.sql already grants them. No DDL: no table, column, constraint, index, trigger, function or policy is created, altered or dropped, RLS state is untouched, and no row is read or written. REVERSIBLE rather than EXPANSION_SAFE because it tightens two pre-existing objects rather than adding new ones; the prior state is restored by a single GRANT per table. Removes anon grants that ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES on the staging database conferred without any migration asking for them, matching the correction already made at source for public.wardrobe_wear_event_items.
